intro: Music: instruments, concerts and the people who make them.
p.el compositor.nota: The feminine form is la compositora.
p.el cantante.nota: The feminine form is la cantante; the ending does not change.
p.el bailarín.nota: The feminine form is la bailarina.
p.en directo.nota: Used in Spain for a live performance or broadcast; en vivo is also common across the Spanish-speaking world.
p.la batería: the drums; the drum kit; the battery
p.tener buen oído: to have a good ear (for music)
p.el músico.nota: The feminine form is la música; in a sentence about a person it means a female musician, while música without an article can mean music.
p.el guitarrista.nota: The feminine form is la guitarrista.
p.el pianista.nota: The feminine form is la pianista.
p.componer.nota: Conjugated like poner: yo compongo, tú compones.
p.el director de orquesta.nota: The feminine form is la directora de orquesta.
b1.texto:
People: **el cantante**, **el compositor**, **el músico**, **el guitarrista**, **el pianista**, **el director de orquesta**, **el bailarín**. Words in **-ista** keep the same ending in the masculine and feminine: **el / la** guitarrista.

You **tocas** an instrument: la guitarra, el piano, el violín, **la batería**. You **cantas**, **bailas**, **compones** and **ensayas**.

A band **saca** un disco, **da** un concierto and **está de gira**. Music played or heard at a concert is **en directo** (or **en vivo**).

A song has **letra** and **música**. A song that becomes very popular is **un éxito**.

To say what music does to you, use the **gustar** pattern: **me emociona**, **me relaja**, **me pone** de buen humor, **me recuerda a** mi infancia.

**Tener buen oído** is to have a good ear. **Saberse** una canción **de memoria** is to know it by heart.
b2.f0: My brother has played the drums in a band for ten years.
b2.f1: They rehearse three times a week in a garage on the outskirts.
b2.f2: The singer composes the music and he writes almost all the lyrics.
b2.f3: Last year they brought out their first album, which was an unexpected hit.
b2.f4: Now they are on tour and give two live concerts every week.
b2.f5: He says that what moves him most is hearing the audience sing their songs.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Jugar is for sports and games.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Hacer is not used with instruments.
b5.pregunta: What are the words of a song called?
b5.o0.refuerzo: La letra means the lyrics, the words written for a song.
b5.o1.refuerzo: The set word is la letra.
b6.o1.explicacion: Estar de gira is to be on tour.
b6.o2: They are out for a walk.
b6.o2.explicacion: Estar de gira is to be on tour.
b7.pregunta: According to the text, who writes the lyrics?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Él escribe casi todas las letras.
b8.pregunta: Complete: this song reminds me of my childhood.
b9.traduccion: They give two live concerts every week.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about a song that matters to you: what it says and what it reminds you of.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Talk aloud about the music you listen to, a concert you remember and an instrument you would like to play.
b6.o0.explicacion: Estar de gira means being on tour, as bands and performers are.
